# Menopause

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Obstetrics/gynecology > Menstrual cycle and associated disorders > Menopause*

[Original Article Link](/library/BO0zuT)

---

## Summary

Menopause is the permanent cessation of <u>menstruation</u> (diagnosed after 12 months of <u>amenorrhea</u>) and is a normal part of the <u>aging</u> process. <u>Perimenopause</u>, sometimes called the <u>menopausal transition</u>, is characterized by gradually decreasing ovarian function resulting in less <u>frequent menstruation</u> and decreased production of <u>female sex hormones</u> until <u>menstruation</u> ceases altogether (usually between 45 and 56 years of age). <u>Induced menopause</u> (due to <u>surgery</u> and <u>chemotherapy</u>) leads to a swift decline in <u>hormones</u>, with menopause occurring earlier and more rapidly compared to <u>physiological menopause</u>. While menopause is defined as an absence of <u>menstruation</u>, it also leads to multiple other physiological changes because of the decline in sex <u>hormones</u>, leading to significant <u>vasomotor symptoms</u>, changes to the genitourinary tract, and neuropsychiatric symptoms (e.g., mood swings, <u>sleep</u> disturbance). In individuals with a characteristic history (e.g., the typical age of menopause with <u>vasomotor symptoms</u> and <u>amenorrhea</u>), a diagnosis of <u>perimenopause</u> or menopause can be made clinically. Diagnostic tests are reserved for individuals with <u>premature menopause</u> (i.e., before the age of 40 years) or if the clinical history requires the exclusion of alternative diagnoses. Nonpharmacological interventions are recommended for mild symptoms. Pharmacological therapy is used for moderate to severe symptoms that impair quality of life and for patients with premature, early, or <u>induced menopause</u> who are at increased risk for <u>complications of menopause</u>.

---

## Definitions

The female reproductive period comprises the following phases: [[1]](/library/V91GmQ0)[[2]](/library/d91omQ0)[[3]](/library/xA1ENj0)




* Premenopause: begins with <u>menarche</u> and ends with the onset of <u>perimenopause</u>

* Perimenopause (also called the <u>menopausal transition</u>): the length of time from the first occurrence of irregular <u>menstruation</u> cycles  ;  to 12 months after the final <u>menstrual period</u> (FMP) [[1]](/library/V91GmQ0)[[2]](/library/d91omQ0)

* Fluctuating hormonal levels lead to increasingly infrequent, lighter <u>menstruation</u> and <u>vasomotor symptoms</u>. [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)[[5]](/library/rbXfE9)

* Duration: variable; median length 4 years [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)

* Menopause: the date of an individual's FMP

* Retroactively determined after 12 months of complete <u>amenorrhea</u> [[1]](/library/V91GmQ0)[[6]](/library/I71YMR0)

* Onset: usually from 45–56 years of age (average is 51 years of age); earlier average age in smokers [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[6]](/library/I71YMR0)[[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[8]](/library/5s1ivR0)

* Physiological menopause is the normal age-related loss of ovarian function with no other identified cause [[2]](/library/d91omQ0)

* Postmenopause: the time after the FMP; the first 12 months are called early <u>postmenopause</u>. [[1]](/library/V91GmQ0)





> [!TIP]
> <u>Perimenopause</u> begins with the onset of irregular <u>menstrual cycles</u>, includes the date of the FMP (i.e., menopause), and ends after the first year of <u>postmenopause</u> (i.e., early <u>postmenopause</u>). [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)[[5]](/library/rbXfE9)

## Physiology of menopause

| <br>Underlying physiology of <u>menopause symptoms</u> [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)[[5]](/library/rbXfE9)<br> |  |
| --- | --- |
| Symptoms | Underlying mechanism |
| <br>Menstrual irregularities and <u>amenorrhea</u> [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)[[5]](/library/rbXfE9)<br> | <br><br>* ↓ Ovarian function from age-related <u>ovarian follicle</u> loss leads to:<br><br>* ↓ <u>Estrogen</u> and <u>progesterone</u> levels → loss of negative feedback on the <u>pituitary gland</u> → ↑ <u>GnRH</u> levels → ↑ <u>FSH</u> and <u>LH</u> levels (<u>hypergonadotropic hypogonadism</u>)<br><br>* ↑ In <u>anovulatory cycles</u><br><br>* Ovarian function eventually ceases.<br><br>* <u>Iatrogenic</u> removal of the <u>ovaries</u> leads to abrupt cessation of ovarian function.<br><br><br> |
| <br><u>Vasomotor symptoms</u> [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)[[5]](/library/rbXfE9)<br> | <br><br>* <u>Hypothalamic</u> <u>thermoregulatory</u> zone narrows → small temperature changes trigger compensatory reactions<br><br>* ↓ <u>Estrogen</u> is associated with ↑ <u>norepinephrine</u> and ↓ <u>serotonin</u><br><br><br> |
| <br>Genitourinary symptoms [[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)<br> | <br>* <u>Hypoestrogenism</u> → vaginal and vulvar <u>epithelial</u> <u>atrophy</u>, as well as urethral and <u>bladder</u> <u>atrophy</u><br><br> |

---

## Clinical features

The onset and intensity of symptoms depend on the phase of menopause and vary greatly between individuals. Symptoms begin during <u>perimenopause</u> and typically peak during the first 1–2 years of <u>postmenopause</u>. [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)




| <br><u>Clinical features of menopause</u> [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)[[5]](/library/rbXfE9)<br> |  |
| --- | --- |
|  | Common symptoms |
| Menstrual abnormalities | <br><br>* Irregular <u>menses</u> that gradually decrease in frequency until complete <u>amenorrhea</u><br><br>* During early <u>perimenopause</u>, cycles may be shorter.  [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)<br><br>* In late <u>perimenopause</u>, cycles are typically longer (≥ 60 days). [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)<br><br>* <u>Heavy menstrual bleeding</u> may occur during <u>perimenopause</u>. [[10]](/library/93WNkO0)<br><br><br> |
| Vasomotor symptoms of menopause (<u>VMS</u>) | <br><br>* Increased sweating<br><br>* <u>Hot flashes</u><br><br>* Heat intolerance<br><br>* Seen in ∼ 75% of individuals during <u>perimenopause</u> and menopause<br><br>* On average, <u>vasomotor symptoms</u> last for ∼ 7 years.  [[6]](/library/I71YMR0)[[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)<br><br><br> |
| <br>Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (<u>GSM</u>) [[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)<br> | <br><br>* Vulvovaginal atrophy leading to:<br><br>* Vaginal dryness<br><br>* <u>Dyspareunia</u><br><br>* Decreasing labial fat pad<br><br>* <u>Pruritus</u><br><br>* <u>Pelvic organ prolapse</u><br><br>* Spotting or bleeding after sex<br><br>* Elevated <u>vaginal pH</u>  [[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)<br><br>* Lower urinary tract atrophy leading to:<br><br>* <u>Dysuria</u><br><br>* <u>Urinary frequency</u> and/or urgency<br><br>* <u>Urinary incontinence</u><br><br>* <u>Recurrent urinary tract infections</u><br><br>* Seen in up to three-quarters of individuals during <u>perimenopause</u> and menopause [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)<br><br>* Symptoms gradually worsen and persist indefinitely.<br><br><br> |
| <br>Neuropsychiatric symptoms [[12]](/library/2s1T8R0)<br> | <br><br>* Impaired <u>sleep</u> (e.g., from <u>insomnia</u> and/or night sweats)<br><br>* <u>Anxiety</u>/irritability<br><br>* Mood swings or <u>depression</u>  [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)<br><br>* <u>Vertigo</u>  [[13]](/library/fjWk-O0)<br><br><br> |
| <br>Other symptoms [[14]](/library/es1xFR0)<br> | <br><br>* Changes to <u>hair</u> distribution<br><br>* <u>Hirsutism</u> (due to a relative increase in <u>androgens</u>) [[6]](/library/I71YMR0)<br><br>* <u>Female pattern hair loss</u> [[14]](/library/es1xFR0)<br><br>* Thinning pubic <u>hair</u> [[15]](/library/ijWJZl0)<br><br>* Decreased libido [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)<br><br>* Weight gain [[14]](/library/es1xFR0)<br><br>* Patients may also present with <u>complications of menopause</u> (e.g., <u>osteoporosis</u>).<br><br><br> |





> [!TIP]
> In the US, more intense and longer-lasting <u>vasomotor symptoms</u> are reported for Black individuals than individuals of other racial or ethnic groups. [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)[[5]](/library/rbXfE9)




![Menopause clinical features](media/vmd3q680y971kxe56954w6m1.jpg)

Menopause clinical features




> [!TIP]
> In menopausal individuals, <u>estrogen</u> production mainly results from the conversion of <u>adrenal</u> <u>androgens</u> by peripheral <u>aromatase</u> in <u>adipose tissue</u>. The onset of menopause may occur later in individuals with <u>obesity</u>, who have additional <u>estrogen</u> from adipose stores. [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)[[16]](/library/pbWLuP0)




> [!NOTE]
> Menopausal HAVOCS: Hot flashes/Heat intolerance, Atrophy of Vagina, Osteoporosis, Coronary <u>artery</u> disease, Sleep impairment.

## Subtypes and variants

### Induced menopause [[2]](/library/d91omQ0)[[6]](/library/I71YMR0)




<u>Induced menopause</u> is the permanent loss of ovarian function as a result of medical interventions.




#### Etiology




* <u>Iatrogenic</u> ovarian <u>ablation</u> (e.g., due to <u>chemotherapy</u>, radiation)

* Surgical menopause: menopause resulting from the removal of both <u>ovaries</u> (i.e., bilateral <u>oophorectomy</u>)





#### Clinical features [[14]](/library/es1xFR0)




* <u>Clinical features of menopause</u> may be more pronounced because of the rapid drop in <u>hormone</u> levels.

* <u>Vasomotor menopause symptoms</u> are more severe and frequent in <u>surgical menopause</u>.





#### Treatment




* <u>Hormone</u> therapy if patients are below the average age of <u>physiological menopause</u> (∼ 51 years of age). [[14]](/library/es1xFR0)

* See also “<u>Treatment of menopause</u>.”





### Premature menopause [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)




<u>Premature menopause</u> is the permanent cessation of ovarian function and <u>menses</u> before the age of 40 years.




#### Etiology




* <u>Induced menopause</u>

* <u>Primary ovarian insufficiency</u>;  (<u>POI</u>): occurs in 1% of women; may be <u>idiopathic</u>  [[6]](/library/I71YMR0)[[17]](/library/tPbXgF)





#### Clinical features




* <u>Clinical features of menopause</u>

* Patients may also present with <u>infertility</u>, or <u>menstrual cycles</u> that do not resume after stopping <u>hormonal contraception</u>. [[18]](/library/dQWoEO0)





#### Diagnostics




* May not be required if the underlying cause is known (e.g., <u>induced menopause</u>)

* If the cause is unknown, <u>diagnostic studies for menopause</u> are recommended.

* Additional <u>workup for POI</u> (e.g., <u>karyotyping</u>) may be required.





#### Treatment




* Hormonal therapy is recommended to reduce:

* <u>Symptoms of menopause</u>

* Risks of <u>early menopause</u>, e.g., increased risk of <u>heart</u> disease, <u>dementia</u>, and increased risk of overall mortality [[14]](/library/es1xFR0)

* Consider <u>oral contraceptive</u> use in patients with no <u>contraindications to combined hormonal contraception</u>. [[14]](/library/es1xFR0)

* Continue systemic <u>HRT</u> (unless contraindicated) until at least the average age of <u>physiological menopause</u> (∼ 51 years of age). [[6]](/library/I71YMR0)[[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)

* See also “<u>Treatment of menopause</u>.”





### Early menopause [[11]](/library/WeXPBC)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)




* The occurrence of <u>physiological menopause</u> between 40 and 45 years of age with no other identified cause  [[11]](/library/WeXPBC)

* Affects 5% of women [[6]](/library/I71YMR0)

* Clinical features and diagnostics are the same as for older patients.

* Systemic <u>HRT</u> is usually recommended to reduce risks associated with <u>early menopause</u>, e.g.: [[14]](/library/es1xFR0)

* Increased risk of <u>heart</u> disease

* <u>Dementia</u>

* Increased risk of overall mortality





> [!TIP]
> Smoking is associated with earlier onset of menopause. [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)[[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[19]](/library/V-1Gwj0)

---

## Diagnosis

### General principles [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)




* In individuals ≥ 40 years of age, <u>perimenopause</u> and menopause are <u>diagnosed clinically</u>.

* A <u>pelvic examination</u> is usually performed to confirm <u>GSM</u> or evaluate for other causes. [[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)

* Diagnostic testing is reserved for:

* <u>Premature menopause</u>

* Patients with an unreliable <u>menstrual cycle</u> history  [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)

* Suspected <u>differential diagnoses of menopause and perimenopause</u>  [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)[[20]](/library/i_1JLj0)





> [!TIP]
> The effects of <u>oral contraceptives</u> can mask the <u>signs and symptoms of menopause</u>. [[21]](/library/q71C5R0)




### Supportive studies to confirm menopause [[1]](/library/V91GmQ0)[[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)




These studies are typically determined by a specialist; there is significant controversy regarding which tests are appropriate.  [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)[[17]](/library/tPbXgF)




* <u>FSH</u>: ↑↑; ; however, levels widely fluctuate during <u>perimenopause</u>  [[1]](/library/V91GmQ0)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)

* <u>Estradiol</u>: ↓ [[1]](/library/V91GmQ0)[[17]](/library/tPbXgF)

* Rarely tested for as not routinely recommended: ↓ <u>progesterone</u>; , ↓ <u>inhibin B</u>, and ↓ antimüllerian <u>hormone</u>  [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)[[6]](/library/I71YMR0)[[22]](/library/7H147R0)





> [!TIP]
> If <u>FSH</u> levels are needed to verify menopause in individuals using <u>oral contraceptives</u>, discontinue <u>oral contraceptives</u> at least 2 weeks prior to testing. [[6]](/library/I71YMR0)[[21]](/library/q71C5R0)




### Studies to exclude <u>differential diagnoses of menopause</u> [[23]](/library/HH1K7R0)




* <u>Pregnancy test</u>: to rule out <u>pregnancy</u> as a cause of <u>amenorrhea</u>  [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)

* <u>Prolactin</u>: elevated in <u>hyperprolactinemia</u>

* <u>LH</u>: elevated in <u>POI</u>

* <u>TSH</u>: Both <u>hypothyroidism</u> and <u>hyperthyroidism</u> can cause menstrual irregularities.

* Tests for <u>hyperandrogenism</u>: <u>testosterone</u>, <u>dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate</u> (<u>DHEA-S</u>), <u>17-hydroxyprogesterone</u> (<u>17-OHP</u>)

* <u>Transvaginal ultrasound</u> +/- <u>endometrial sampling</u> if <u>endometrial cancer</u> is suspected  [[24]](/library/g21FST0)





> [!TIP]
> Individuals with <u>hyperthyroidism</u> and menopause have similar symptoms. Maintain a low threshold for checking serum <u>TSH</u> in individuals with heat intolerance, irregular <u>menstruation</u>, and disturbed <u>sleep</u>. [[23]](/library/HH1K7R0)




### Studies for <u>complications of menopause</u>




These studies are not routinely part of the menopause workup but if performed, findings may show characteristic changes.




* <u>Lipid panel</u>: ↑ total <u>cholesterol</u> and ↓ <u>HDL</u> are common during menopause

* <u>DXA scan</u>: recommended for all women aged ≥ 65 years and younger women with additional <u>risk factors</u> (see “<u>Screening for osteoporosis</u>”)  [[25]](/library/SQWyvO0)[[26]](/library/uHXpHz)

* May show <u>osteopenia</u> or <u>osteoporosis</u>

* Significant <u>bone mineral density</u> is lost over a 3-year period around the FMP.  [[27]](/library/WQWPEO0)

---

## Treatment

The information in this section is on the management of <u>physiological menopause</u> in individuals aged > 45 years. For the management of <u>premature menopause</u>, <u>early menopause</u>, and <u>induced menopause</u>, see “Subtypes and variants.”




### Approach [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)




* Determine the severity of symptoms and their impact on the patient's quality of life.

* All symptomatic patients: Initiate <u>symptom-specific nonpharmacological interventions for menopause</u>.

* For patients with moderate to severe symptoms, consider adding <u>pharmacological therapy for menopause</u>.  [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[30]](/library/z_1rIj0)

* For <u>perimenopausal</u> individuals, discuss <u>contraception during perimenopause</u>.

* Screen for and treat associated conditions and/or complications and provide appropriate preventive care.

* <u>Screen for depression</u>.

* Educate patients on the increased risk of <u>osteoporosis</u> and <u>heart</u> disease and initiate:

* <u>Primary prevention of ASCVD</u>

* <u>Prevention of osteoporosis</u>





> [!TIP]
> Questionnaires, e.g., the menopause-specific quality of life scale, may help to determine the severity of symptoms and guide treatment.




> [!TIP]
> <u>Hormone replacement therapy</u> is not indicated for all patients but should be prescribed for <u>premature menopause</u>, <u>early menopause</u>, and patients with moderate to severe <u>symptoms of menopause</u>. [[11]](/library/WeXPBC)

---

For further information on indications, contraindications, and dosages, see “<u>Pharmacological therapy for menopause</u>.”

|  | Symptom-specific nonpharmacological interventions for menopause | Symptom-specific <u>pharmacological therapy for menopause</u> |

| <br>Psychological symptoms [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)[[32]](/library/Us1b8R0)<br> | <br><br>* <u>Cognitive behavioral therapy</u> (first-line) [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)<br><br>* Relaxation techniques<br><br>* <u>Sleep hygiene</u><br><br>* Exercise<br><br><br> | <br>* Treatment as indicated, e.g.:<br><br>* <u>Treatment for depression</u><br><br>* <u>Treatment of anxiety disorders</u><br><br>* <u>Pharmacotherapy for insomnia</u><br><br> |
| <br>Other [[8]](/library/5s1ivR0)<br> | <br><br>* Weight gain [[6]](/library/I71YMR0)<br><br>* Dietary changes<br><br>* Increase exercise.<br><br>* Behavioral support<br><br>* <u>Hirsutism</u>: <u>hair</u> removal  [[6]](/library/I71YMR0)[[33]](/library/cB1a-Q0)<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Decreased libido: Consider <u>testosterone</u> (<u>off-label</u>).  [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)<br><br>* <u>Hirsutism</u>: Consider <u>antiandrogens</u>.  [[33]](/library/cB1a-Q0)<br><br><br> |





> [!TIP]
> Evidence does not support the use of alternative medical therapies for menopause, e.g., soy, black cohosh, <u>omega-3</u> supplementation, and <u>acupuncture</u>. [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)

## Pharmacological therapy for menopause

### Systemic hormone replacement therapy (<u>HRT</u>) [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)




#### General principles




* <u>HRT</u> should be titrated to the lowest effective dose.  [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)

* Reevaluate patients on <u>HRT</u> yearly. [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)

* Short-term use (< 5 years) may be preferred to reduce the risk of adverse effects (e.g., <u>breast cancer</u>).  [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)[[34]](/library/RQWlDO0)





#### Indications [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)




* <u>Premature menopause</u>, <u>induced menopause</u>, or <u>early menopause</u>

* Moderate to severe <u>vasomotor symptoms</u> affecting quality of life if both criteria are met : [[11]](/library/WeXPBC)

* < 60 years of age

* Menopausal for < 10 years

* Moderate to severe genitourinary <u>symptoms of menopause</u>  [[14]](/library/es1xFR0)

* <u>Prevention of osteoporosis</u> in <u>postmenopausal</u> individuals (controversial)  [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)[[30]](/library/z_1rIj0)[[35]](/library/H_1Kpj0)





> [!TIP]
> Multiple medical societies do not recommend systemic <u>HRT</u> solely for the prevention of chronic diseases (e.g., <u>osteoporosis</u> and cardiovascular diseases) in menopausal individuals. [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[30]](/library/z_1rIj0)




#### Options for HRT  [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)[[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)




* Systemic <u>estrogen</u> hormonal options include oral and transdermal preparations.

* Transdermal preparations may have a lower risk of <u>VTE</u> and cardiovascular disease.  [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)

* Patients without a <u>uterus</u>: estrogen-only HRT

* Micronized 17β-<u>estradiol</u> DOSAGE  [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)

* Conjugated <u>estrogen</u> DOSAGE [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)

* Transdermal 17β-<u>estradiol</u> gel DOSAGE OR patch DOSAGE  [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)

* Patients with a <u>uterus</u>: <u>estrogen</u>-containing <u>HRT</u> combined with an <u>endometrial</u> protection agent

* Combined estrogen-progestin HRT preparations, e.g.:

* Conjugated <u>estrogen</u>/<u>medroxyprogesterone acetate</u> DOSAGE [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)

* 17β-<u>estradiol</u>/<u>norethindrone</u> acetate patch DOSAGE or pill DOSAGE [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)

* <u>Estrogen</u> PLUS an <u>SERM</u>, e.g., conjugated <u>estrogen</u> DOSAGE PLUS bazedoxifene DOSAGE [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)

* <u>Estrogen-only HRT</u> plus a <u>levonorgestrel-releasing IUD</u> (<u>off-label</u>)  [[14]](/library/es1xFR0)





> [!TIP]
> Unopposed systemic <u>estrogen</u> can increase the risk of <u>endometrial hyperplasia</u> and <u>endometrial cancer</u>. In individuals with a <u>uterus</u>, add an agent that protects the <u>endometrium</u> (e.g., <u>progestins</u>, bazedoxifene). [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)




> [!WARNING]
> Some clinicians prescribe compounded <u>bioidentical hormones</u>; however, these are not <u>FDA</u>-approved and are not recommended by any major societies as there is no evidence they are superior to standard <u>HRT</u>. [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)




#### Contraindications to HRT [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)




* Unexplained <u>vaginal bleeding</u>

* <u>Estrogen</u>-sensitive cancer (e.g., <u>endometrial</u> or <u>breast cancer</u>)

* <u>Chronic liver disease</u>

* Current or prior <u>DVT</u>, <u>stroke</u>, thromboembolic disease, or <u>thrombophilia</u>

* <u>Coronary artery disease</u> or <u>myocardial infarction</u>





#### Adverse effects [[14]](/library/es1xFR0)




* Serious: <u>thromboembolic events</u>, <u>estrogen</u>-sensitive cancer (e.g., <u>endometrial cancer</u>, <u>breast cancer</u>)  [[14]](/library/es1xFR0)[[34]](/library/RQWlDO0)

* Common: mood swings, <u>headache</u>, gastrointestinal upset (e.g., <u>nausea</u>, <u>bloating</u>), weight gain, retained fluid, <u>breast</u> <u>pain</u>, <u>breakthrough bleeding</u>

* Other: <u>stress urinary incontinence</u>, <u>gallbladder</u> disease





### Vaginal hormone therapy [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)




<u>Vaginal hormone therapy</u> is indicated for moderate to severe genitourinary <u>symptoms of menopause</u>.




#### Options




* <u>Estrogen</u>-based intravaginal treatments ;  [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)[[11]](/library/WeXPBC)

* Creams, e.g., conjugated <u>estrogen</u> DOSAGE OR <u>estradiol</u> DOSAGE [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)

* Gel capsules, e.g., <u>estradiol</u> DOSAGE [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)

* Rings, e.g., <u>estradiol</u> DOSAGE [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)

* Intravaginal <u>DHEA</u>, i.e., vaginal prasterone DOSAGE [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)





#### Contraindications [[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)




* Undiagnosed <u>vaginal bleeding</u>

* <u>Estrogen</u>-sensitive cancers (e.g., <u>endometrial</u> or <u>breast cancer</u>)  [[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)

* History of a prior <u>thromboembolic event</u>  [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)

* <u>Liver</u> disease  [[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)





> [!TIP]
> In consultation with oncology, low-dose vaginal <u>estrogen</u> may be considered in individuals with a history of <u>breast cancer</u>. [[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)[[31]](/library/Ft1g2i0)




> [!NOTE]
> Despite the <u>FDA</u> boxed warning applying to all <u>estrogen</u> products, the clinical evidence supports the use of low-dose vaginal <u>estrogen</u> for symptomatic relief in women with prior <u>venous thromboembolism</u>, as systemic absorption is insufficient to alter <u>coagulation parameters</u> or increase clotting risk. [[36]](/library/rOVfFu0)




#### Adverse effects [[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)




* Risk of <u>estrogen</u>-sensitive cancers and <u>thromboembolic events</u>; however, risk is lower than for systemic <u>HRT</u>  [[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)

* <u>Vaginal discharge</u>, <u>candidiasis</u>, or bleeding





> [!WARNING]
> As low-dose vaginal <u>estrogen</u> is generally not associated with <u>endometrial hyperplasia</u>, additional <u>progestin</u> is typically not added for <u>endometrial</u> protection. However, patients should be advised to immediately report any <u>vaginal bleeding</u>. [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[14]](/library/es1xFR0)




### Nonhormonal therapy [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)[[31]](/library/Ft1g2i0)




#### Indications




* Alternative treatment for patients who decline, or have contraindications to, <u>HRT</u>

* Second-line treatment for moderate to severe menopausal symptoms





#### Options




* <u>Vasomotor symptoms</u>

* Fezolinetant DOSAGE

* <u>Paroxetine</u> DOSAGE  [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[21]](/library/q71C5R0)

* <u>Gabapentin</u> (<u>off-label</u>) DOSAGE [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)

* <u>Clonidine</u> (<u>off-label</u>) DOSAGE [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)

* Genitourinary symptoms: a <u>SERM</u>, e.g., <u>ospemifene</u> DOSAGE  [[5]](/library/rbXfE9)[[7]](/library/LaWwOP0)[[9]](/library/fG1kAR0)[[21]](/library/q71C5R0)

* Benign <u>hirsutism</u>: <u>antiandrogen therapy</u>  [[6]](/library/I71YMR0)[[37]](/library/3_1SLj0)

---

## Complications

* <u>Coronary artery disease</u>

* <u>Estrogen</u> exerts protective effects on the <u>cardiovascular system</u>.  [[40]](/library/G_1Bpj0)

* Menopause is associated with increased <u>triglycerides</u>, <u>LDL</u>, weight gain, and <u>hypertension</u>. [[8]](/library/5s1ivR0)

* <u>Osteoporosis</u>: Decreased circulating <u>estrogen</u> impairs bone formation. [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)





### Associated conditions




* <u>Postmenopausal bleeding</u>

* <u>Vaginal bleeding</u> after menopause requires evaluation to rule out <u>malignancy</u>. [[41]](/library/ce1aBf0)

* See “<u>Approach to postmenopausal bleeding</u>” for details.

* <u>Unplanned pregnancy</u>: <u>Ovulation</u>, though infrequent, still occurs during <u>perimenopause</u> (see also “<u>Contraception during perimenopause</u>”. [[4]](/library/i71JlR0)





We list the most important complications. The selection is not exhaustive.
